obligations: Apache-2.0 requires that redistributions include a copy of the license, retain attribution/copyright notices, mark modified files, and include the NOTICE file attribution text where applicable (Apache-2.0 sections 4(a)-(d) in repository LICENSE).
NOTICE requires attribution to Microsoft Corporation and disclosure that code is derived from the Puppeteer project under Apache-2.0.

Vendored/bundled third-party code carries its own licenses: MIT for VSCode web components (packages/web/src/third_party/vscode/LICENSE.txt) and the test proxy (node-http-proxy, tests/third_party/proxy/LICENSE); Apache-2.0 for the BIDI protocol client (playwright-core/src/server/bidi/third_party/LICENSE). Package-level third-party notices documented in packages/playwright/ThirdPartyNotices.txt.
rationale: The repository root LICENSE is the complete Apache License 2.0 text. Root package.json declares "license": "Apache-2.0" and every sub-package manifest that declares a license field (playwright, playwright-core, playwright-test, playwright-chromium/firefox/webkit, browser-* binaries, ct-* packages) is Apache-2.0, with no conflicting package-level license. Apache-2.0 is an OSI-approved permissive license with no copyleft or proprietary constraints, so the result is PASS. No material copyleft or proprietary constraint was identified in the audited tree; bundled/vendored third-party components are MIT or Apache-2.0, both permissive and compatible. Caveat: individual bundled output files under packages/playwright/lib/ each carry a sidecar *.js.LICENSE file listing inlined npm packages (per ThirdPartyNotices.txt); these were not exhaustively enumerated, so a full dependency-graph license sweep of transitively bundled npm deps would be needed for an exhaustive obligation inventory, but nothing found contradicts the Apache-2.0 determination.
